analysis.summary: MapView's mount effect enumerates all domains of the loaded footprints and calls fetchBulkGeolocation for every uncached one — unconditionally, on dashboard open. The fetch targets GEO_API_URL = 'http://ip-api.com/json/' (cleartext) in both src/dashboard/utils/geolocation.js and its service-worker twin src/lib/geo-queue.js, so opening the dashboard silently leaks the user's full visited-domain list to a third party over plain HTTP — directly contradicting the privacy-first product premise. Separately, MapView.jsx builds Leaflet popup HTML via template-literal string interpolation of location.city/region/country and domain strings before bindPopup, an HTML-injection surface fed by external geo data.
analysis.details: Failure chain: dashboard opens -> MapView useEffect -> uniqueDomains from footprints -> fetchBulkGeolocation(uncached) -> http://ip-api.com (cleartext, no user consent, contradicting zero-telemetry copy). The extension history introduced this with the v1.2.0 Map View release (7eaa9ea); it is not a regression but a design flaw. The fix has three inseparable parts per the issue: (1) gate the default path — no fetch of http://ip-api.com unless the user opts in (or switch to HTTPS / remove live lookups); (2) sanitize popup HTML so geo/domain strings are never interpolated unescaped; (3) update the dashboard footer and privacy-policy.md in the same change so the copy cannot lie about the behavior. A unit test asserting the default path does not fetch is the acceptance seam; tests/unit/geolocation.test.js and tests/unit/geo-queue.test.js already exist as hosts. Note src/lib/geo-queue.js is the SW twin slated for removal by #32 (3.4) — do not invest in it beyond the security fix.
analysis.reproduction_note: grep confirms `const GEO_API_URL = 'http://ip-api.com/json/'` in both geolocation.js:17 and geo-queue.js:10, and MapView.jsx auto-fetches uncached domains on mount without an opt-in gate.
